chunks: 4097 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an item in the hands of two men: one of them says, "I entrusted it to you as a deposit," and the other says, "It is a pledge with me." So he said, "The statement is the statement of the one who says, 'It is a pledge with me,' unless the one who claimed that he had deposited it brings witnesses."

key_terms.اسْتَوْدَعْتُكَهُ: I entrusted it to you as a deposit for safekeeping
key_terms.الْقَوْلُ: the legally accepted statement or claim in the dispute
key_terms.رَهْنٌ: a pledged item held as collateral
key_terms.مَتَاعٍ: property or an item of possession under dispute

ai.seo_question: In a dispute over whether property is a deposit or a pledge, whose claim is accepted in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a dispute over property, where one party claims the item was deposited for safekeeping and the other claims it was given as a pledge. The ruling accepts the claim of pledge unless the claimant of deposit establishes his case through witnesses, highlighting evidentiary standards in financial disputes.
